sentences.text: Scelidosaurus was a lightly armored, quadrupedal herbivore that lived during the Jurassic period in England.
This dinosaur reached a length of approximately 4 meters and possessed a torso that was relatively flat in side view and taller than wide.
Its snout was flat on top and largely formed by nasal bones, while the premaxillae bore a small upper beak in life.
The most obvious feature of the animal was its armor, which consisted of bony scutes embedded in the skin.
In 2020, Norman identified unique bones covering the nasal cavity roof called epivomers, which are not known from any other animal.
The osteoderms of Scelidosaurus varied in size and shape, with most being oval plates featuring a high keel on the outside where the highest point was positioned toward the rear.
Scelidosaurus has been called the first complete dinosaur, a claim also made for Compsognathus.
James Harrison discovered Scelidosaurus fossils in the Black Ven cliffs of Charmouth, West Dorset, England during the 1850s.
Richard Owen named and described the dinosaur Scelidosaurus in 1859 following these initial fossil finds.
Sir Richard Owen classified Scelidosaurus within the Dinosauria in 1861.
In 1888, R. Lydekker cataloged numerous single bones, mostly limb elements and osteoderms, acquired by the Natural History Museum, London, from the Norris collection.
David Norman concluded Scelidosaurus fed on low scrubby vegetation up to one meter in height.
Pollen evidence suggests conifers of the extinct family Cheirolepidiaceae grew on the Early Jurassic islands of Europe where Scelidosaurus lived.
Researchers believe Scelidosaurus fed by crushing food between its teeth using a simple up-and-down jaw movement.
Richard Owen hypothesized in 1861 that Scelidosaurus was a fish-eater that partially lived in the sea, a view that differs from modern interpretations.
Richard Owen speculated that Scelidosaurus might have been ovoviviparous based on its relatively large size and presumed marine lifestyle.
A trackway from the Holy Cross Mountains in Poland shows a Scelidosaurus-like animal walking bipedally, suggesting it may have been more competent at bipedalism than previously thought.
The exact placement of Scelidosaurus within the thyreophoran group has been debated for nearly 150 years.
It is debated whether the family Scelidosauridae is paraphyletic or monophyletic, with Benton (2004) arguing for the latter.
Although fragmentary fossils led to a reassessment placing S. oehleri in Scelidosaurus, this view was not accepted, and it is now recognized as Tatisaurus.
It is debated whether the misidentified knee joint specimen belongs to Scelidosaurus or to a member of the Coelophysoidea or Neoceratosauria.
Scelidosaurus belongs to the parent group Scelidosauridae, which is its family, and it is classified in the class Ornithischia.
Scelidosaurus lived approximately 191 million years ago during the Early Jurassic epoch.
Scelidosaurus lived approximately 196 to 183 million years ago during the Early Jurassic in what is now Europe.
Scelidosaurus and related genera lived on the supercontinent Laurasia during the Early Jurassic.
